refutedOnReview: REFUTED. All three cited PDFs exist and were downloaded and text-extracted (pdftotext), but they do not say what the claim says.  **1. Appendix B is not a register table — it is an inverter compatibility list.** Its actual title is "Apéndice B: Protocolo de soporte para inversores" (Supported protocol for inverters). Its RS485 section does have exactly 18 entries — so the "18-entry" count is numerically right — but t
gotchas: THE RACK MANUAL'S RS485-TO-INVERTER PINOUT IS WRONG AS PRINTED. Table 3.6.3-3, headed 'Comunicación independiente RS485', lists pin 4 = CAN-H and pin 5 = CAN-L — byte-for-byte the CAN table 3.6.3-2 above it. An RS485 port has no CAN-H. The Powerwall manual V2.7 gives the port correctly as 1,8 = RS485-B1; 2,7 = RS485-A1
The label 'Tabla 3.6.3-3' is used for two different tables in the rack manual (the RS485 pinout and the communication-cable list). Cite by page, not by table number.
The inverter-facing RS485 port and the parallel-cluster RS485-1/2 ports are different connectors. Plugging a gateway into RS485-1 puts it on the inter-pack bus, where the master is already polling.

The default 'PYLON RS485 LV-BPB V3.5-2019.08.07' is a Pylontech document Cabin Hub does not hold. The version and date are recorded because BSLBATT states them; the registers are not, because nobody has read them.
9600 bps is stated repeatedly and the wall manual's LCD says 'Baud Rate: 9600, Can not be set.' Parity/stop bits are nowhere. Left null.
unmappedReports: Same set as the CAN dialect: fault/alarm code, reported CCL/DCL, pack index, MOSFET temperature, cluster size., Dry-contact alarm outputs. The wall manual defines pin1–pin2 as normally open and closing on break/protection, and pin3–pin4 as normally open and closing on low-SOC alarm. MetricKind::SwitchState is a boolean but means 'is this switch closed', not 'is this alarm relay asserted'; there is no alarm-output kind and no way to say which alarm.
